leads.title: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (Bill C-150) - Parliament of Canada
leads.documents: Federal decriminalization of same-sex sexual activity in private between consenting adults, brought into force June 27, 1969 - foundational criminal legal status applicable in Newfoundland and Labrador.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible in text: 'Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968–69 (also known as Bill C-150) was brought into force upon royal assent' and 'decriminalized sexual activity between men, with a higher age of consent, set at 21 years.' No URL visible in excerpt.

leads.title: Egan v. Canada, [1995] - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Landmark ruling that sexual orientation is constitutionally protected under s.15 equality clause of the Canadian Charter as an analogous ground - provides constitutional equality framework enforceable in Newfoundland and Labrador.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: 'In a landmark decision in 1995, Egan v Canada, the Supreme Court of Canada held that sexual orientation is constitutionally protected under the equality clause' and 'declared that sexual orientation was included within the bounds of section 15, as an analogous ground.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Vriend v Alberta, [1998] - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Held failure of provincial legislature to include sexual orientation as prohibited ground in human rights law was itself a violation of s.15 Charter rights - led to requirement that all provinces/territories including Newfoundland and Labrador cover sexual orientation and later gender identity.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: 'In its 1998 decision in Vriend v Alberta, the Supreme Court found the failure of the provincial legislature to include sexual orientation as a prohibited ground of discrimination in its human rights law was itself a violation of section 15 Charter rights.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, s.15(1), s.1, s.33 - Constitution of Canada
leads.documents: Constitutional equality guarantee, reasonable limits (Oakes Test), and notwithstanding clause mechanics; s.15 applies to all laws and government institutions including law enforcement in Newfoundland and Labrador; guides interpretation of human rights laws.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: Full quote of '15(1) Every individual is equal before and under the law...' plus discussion of section 1 and section 33, and 'Section 15 applies to all laws and government institutions in Canada, including law enforcement authorities.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Civil Marriage Act (2005) and 2004 Supreme Court Reference re Same-Sex Marriage - Parliament / Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Federal legalization of same-sex marriage nationwide July 20, 2005, after Supreme Court December 2004 opinion that proposed definition was consistent with Charter and within exclusive federal authority - establishes marriage equality in Newfoundland and Labrador.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: 'on July 20, 2005, Canada became the first country outside Europe and the fourth country in the world to legalize same-sex marriage nationwide after the enactment of the federal Civil Marriage Act' and 'In December 2004, the Supreme Court declared the proposed definition of "marriage" as being consistent...' No URL visible.

leads.title: Newfoundland and Labrador same-sex adoption legalization (2002) - provincial adoption statutes
leads.documents: Specifically documents family/parental rights in Newfoundland and Labrador: joint/stepchild adoption by same-sex couples legalized in 2002 as part of cross-Canada list.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: 'adoption by same-sex couples has been legalized in... Newfoundland and Labrador (2002)...' No statute name or URL visible in excerpt.

leads.title: Federal and provincial human rights acts - prohibition of discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity (as of 2017)
leads.documents: Documents anti-discrimination and anti-harassment machinery covering employment, housing, public/private accommodations: all provinces, territories and federal government explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity, which includes Newfoundland and Labrador; plus division of jurisdiction explanation for Canadian Human Rights Act vs provincial laws.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: 'As of 2017, all provinces, territories, and the federal government explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity as prohibited grounds of discrimination in their human rights acts.' and 'Discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity or expression in employment, housing and public and private accommodations is now prohibited by all provinces and territories.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act (2018) - Parliament of Canada / Parole Board of Canada
leads.documents: Remedial rights machinery for historically criminalized homosexual acts and anal intercourse under repealed s.159: allows RCMP/federal departments and provincial/municipal police/courts to destroy/remove judicial records; explains expungement vs pardon.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: 'On June 21, 2018, the Governor General granted royal assent to the Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act (French: Loi sur la radiation de condamnations constituant des injustices historiques).' plus Parole Board statement quoted. No URL visible.

leads.title: Court Challenges Program - Federal Government
leads.documents: Documents enforcement/access-to-justice machinery: federal funding expanded in 1985 to fund test cases challenging federal legislation on Charter equality rights, with varying provincial programs - mechanism behind LGBTQ s.15 litigation applicable to Newfoundland and Labrador.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: 'Some of the cases were funded under the Federal Government's Court Challenges Program, which in 1985 was expanded to fund test cases challenging federal legislation in relation to the equality rights guaranteed by the Charter.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police formal apology (December 2020)
leads.documents: Institutional law-enforcement acknowledgment of decades of oppression, institutional bias and human rights violations against Two-spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer communities, and creation of Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Committee - relevant to policing/enforcement climate for trans visitors across Canada including Newfoundland and Labrador.
leads.detail: Citation detail visible: 'In December 2020, Police chiefs of Canada made a formal apology – for the decades of oppression and opposition towards homosexuality and LGBTQ rights...' with full quoted apology. No URL visible.
